newsitem.title: UK: St Petersburg's first Eurobond oversubscribed.
newsitem.headline: St Petersburg's first Eurobond oversubscribed.

text.p: The City of St Petersburg launched its first Eurobond on Thursday which was oversubscribed following extensive investor presentations across Asia, Europe and the U.S
"Buying has been global which shows the strength of the demand for this credit, and for Russian paper in general," a syndicate source close to the deal said.
The $300 million five-year bond was priced to yield 312.5 basis points over U.S. Treasury notes and pays a coupon of 9.50 percent.

"The purpose of this issue is to refinance with longer maturity and lower cost a portion of the City's domestic Rouble short-term debt," lead manager for the transaction Salomon Brothers said in a statement.
St Petersburg -- Russia's second largest city -- is rated BB- by Standard and Poor's and BB+ by IBCA.
"This historic transaction marks the City's return to the international markets after more than 80 years," St Petersburg governor Vladimir Yakovlev said in the statement issued by Salomon.
"It reflects the government of St Petersburg's commitment to market transformation in Russia... including privatisation, land, securities markets and the public housing sector."
On May 27 the City of Moscow launched its first Eurobond which was hailed a huge success.
The $500 million May 2000 bond was priced to yield 315 b.p. over U.S. Treasury notes and was last trading at around 282 b.p. over, dealers said.
Russia's $1.0 billion five-year bond was launched last November to yield 345 b.p. over U.S. Treasury notes and was now also trading at around 282 b.p, dealers said.
